embedding.label: The problem
embedding.caption: But the customer said ‘money back,’ and the document says ‘refund.’ Not a single word matches, so nothing comes up.

embedding.label: What it is
embedding.caption: An embedding turns each sentence into a list of numbers, like coordinates on a map. Sentences that mean similar things land close together: refund, money back, I want to return this.

embedding.label: How it's used
embedding.caption: Prep: turn every document, chunk by chunk, into a point, and store them. When a customer asks something, turn the question into a point too. Find the nearest: grab the few chunks closest to it, and hand them to the AI to answer.

embedding.label: The business
embedding.caption: Model makers sell it, databases store it, and software companies build it into their products.

embedding.label: One line to remember
embedding.caption: So remember it in one line: an embedding turns things into meaning coordinates. Once you have them, you can find things by meaning.

vector-database.label: The problem
vector-database.caption: That one question alone takes more than 10 billion multiplications. With a few thousand customers asking at once, the servers can't keep up.

vector-database.label: What it is
vector-database.caption: What it is: it stores points, and it can quickly find the few closest to any given point. What it's used for: support bots looking up documents, searching by image, recommending similar products.

vector-database.label: How it finds fast
vector-database.caption: Take the train to the right city, the subway to the right neighbourhood, then walk the last few steps to the door. Along the way it only looks at a small share of the points, and still finds the closest few.

vector-database.label: The business
vector-database.caption: In the middle is the warehouse, and three groups are crowding in.

vector-database.label: One line to remember
vector-database.caption: One line to remember: a vector database is a warehouse that stores points, and can quickly find the few closest ones.

rag.label: The problem
rag.caption: Two problems: the answer is out of date, and it can't say where it came from. RAG fixes exactly those two.

rag.label: What it is
rag.caption: The RAG idea is simple: first find the few relevant passages in your documents, then have the AI answer from them. Think of an open-book exam. The AI is the smart student, and RAG lets it look things up in the book before it answers.

rag.label: How it works
rag.caption: Pinecone's intro article breaks it into four steps: ingest, retrieve, augment, which means building it into the prompt, and finally, generate.

rag.label: The business
rag.caption: And at the top, the apps that sell answers directly: Glean for company search, Harvey for law, Hebbia for finance.

rag.label: One line to remember
rag.caption: One line to remember: RAG means retrieve first, then generate. It lets the AI take an open-book exam.
